name: Third Battle of Panipat

phases.title: The two lines face each other
phases.text: The Maratha lines stood a little north of Kala Amb with Bhau and the royal guard in the centre, the Gardis on the left and Holkar and Sindhia on the right. The Afghan line stood to the south with Najib on its left and the Rohillas on its right centre.

phases.title: The Gardis advance
phases.text: The Maratha left, under Ibrahim Khan, advanced its infantry in formation against the Rohillas and Shah Pasand Khan. The first salvos from the Maratha artillery went over the Afghans' heads and did little damage.

phases.title: The first Afghan attack breaks and the Rohillas fall back
phases.text: The first Afghan attack was broken by Maratha bowmen, pikemen and Gardi musketeers. Later salvos at point-blank range sent the Rohillas reeling back, and the Gardis held the field for three hours.

phases.title: Bhau charges the Afghan left centre
phases.text: Bhau led a charge against the forces under Shah Wali. The attack nearly broke the Afghan lines, but Shuja-ud-Daulah did not move from his position and the Maratha mounts were exhausted.

phases.title: Scindia attacks Najib
phases.text: The Marathas under Scindia attacked Najib on the Afghan left. Najib fought a defensive action and kept Scindia's forces at bay, so that the Afghan left flank still held its own.

phases.title: Ahmad Shah calls up his reserve
phases.text: Ahmad Shah, who had watched the battle from his tent, sent his bodyguards to call up his 15,000 reserve troops from his camp. He arranged them as a column in front of his cavalry of musketeers.

phases.title: Part of the reserve goes to the Rohillas
phases.text: By then the Afghan right was almost destroyed. Ahmad Shah sent 4,000 of his reserve troops to support the broken ranks of the Rohillas on the right.

phases.title: The rest of the reserve charges with Shah Wali
phases.text: The remaining 10,000 of the reserve were sent to the aid of Shah Wali against Bhau in the centre. Some 7,000 Maratha cavalry and infantry were killed before the hand-to-hand fighting began.

phases.title: The Maratha cavalry breaks its position
phases.text: The cavalry that Bhau had ordered to protect the Gardis broke its position and went all out on the Rohillas. The Rohilla riflemen fired accurately on it, as it carried only swords.

phases.title: The Gardis are encircled
phases.text: The Rohillas then encircled the Gardis and outflanked the Maratha centre while Shah Wali pressed the front. The Gardis were left defenceless and fell one by one.

phases.title: Holkar and Scindia leave the field
phases.text: Realising the battle was lost, Holkar's and Scindia's contingents merged, and one broke from the Maratha right and escaped south through an opening in the Durrani lines. Bhau and the royal forces fought on.

note: The Marathas blocked the Afghans' northward path and were themselves blocked from going south, so they are drawn to the north and the Afghans to the south. The Maratha left is then the east and the Afghan left the west. The accounts differ in places: Pasand Khan is placed both on the Afghan left wing and against the Maratha left, and which Rohillas fell back first is not clear, so the Rohillas of the Afghan right centre are shown. The kind of troops of Holkar and Sindhia and the route of the contingent that escaped are not given, and the positions of the cavalry under Vinchurkar and Gaikwad are placed by judgement. The line is drawn short; the accounts give the Maratha line as some 12 km across. The 4,000 reserve troops sent to the Rohillas are drawn between the reserve and the Rohillas; the accounts do not say which way they came.
